consulted.title: Installing Pytorch with Python 3.10 for CUDA on NVIDIA TITAN BLACK - TITAN - NVIDIA Developer Forums
consulted.content:
Root cause: conda-forge gcc8’s target triplet is `x86_64-conda-linux-gnu`, its own sysroot doesn’t include Ubuntu’s real `/usr/include`. `--sysroot=/` alone breaks other headers in cascade. Fix: wrapper adds `-isystem /usr/include` only when compiling a file that references `python3.10` (avoid touching the ~750 already-compiled objects against the conda sysroot).

`x86_64-conda-linux-gnu`
`/usr/include`
`--sysroot=/`
`-isystem /usr/include`
`python3.10` [...] Note: when reconfiguring with `cmake ..`, pass BOTH `-DCUDA_HOST_COMPILER=` (PyTorch’s own var) AND `-DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=` (native CMake var) → both must point to the gcc8 wrapper. One without the other is not enough.

`cmake ..`
`-DCUDA_HOST_COMPILER=`
`-DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=`

## Problems hit and fixed

### 1. CUDA 10.2 rejects host compiler > GCC 8 [...] Compiled PyTorch 1.12.1 from source with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=3.5` for a GTX Titan Black (Kepler, sm\_35) under WSL2 / Ubuntu 24.04. Official PyPI wheels (1.12.1+cu113, +cu102) do NOT work anymore — Kepler kernels dropped from official builds (`CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device`). Only fix: compile from source. Working `.whl` produced and validated: `torch.cuda.is_available() == True`, matmul on GPU OK.

consulted.content:
```

```

The PyTorch CUDA version must not exceed the driver CUDA version. If it does, either upgrade your driver or install an older PyTorch build. See our tutorials for the compatibility matrix.

## Fix 3: Enable GPU Access in Docker [...] 1. CPU-only PyTorch installed. The default `pip install torch` may install the CPU build if no index URL is specified.
2. CUDA toolkit version mismatch. PyTorch was compiled against CUDA 12.1, but your driver only supports up to CUDA 11.8.
3. NVIDIA driver not loaded. The kernel module is missing or blacklisted.
4. Running inside a container without GPU passthrough. Docker needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. [...] If `nvidia-smi` itself fails, the issue is at the driver level — our guide on installing NVIDIA CUDA covers driver installation from scratch. If `nvidia-smi` works but `torch.version.cuda` prints `None`, you have a CPU-only PyTorch build.

## Fix 1: Replace CPU-Only PyTorch with GPU Build

This is the most common cause. Uninstall and reinstall with the correct CUDA index:

```
pip uninstall torch torchvision torchaudio -y pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url 
```

consulted.title: Installing Pytorch with Python 3.10 for CUDA on NVIDIA TITAN BLACK - TITAN - NVIDIA Developer Forums
consulted.content:
Root cause: conda-forge gcc8’s target triplet is `x86_64-conda-linux-gnu`, its own sysroot doesn’t include Ubuntu’s real `/usr/include`. `--sysroot=/` alone breaks other headers in cascade. Fix: wrapper adds `-isystem /usr/include` only when compiling a file that references `python3.10` (avoid touching the ~750 already-compiled objects against the conda sysroot).

`x86_64-conda-linux-gnu`
`/usr/include`
`--sysroot=/`
`-isystem /usr/include`
`python3.10` [...] Note: when reconfiguring with `cmake ..`, pass BOTH `-DCUDA_HOST_COMPILER=` (PyTorch’s own var) AND `-DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=` (native CMake var) → both must point to the gcc8 wrapper. One without the other is not enough.

`cmake ..`
`-DCUDA_HOST_COMPILER=`
`-DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=`

## Problems hit and fixed

### 1. CUDA 10.2 rejects host compiler > GCC 8 [...] Compiled PyTorch 1.12.1 from source with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=3.5` for a GTX Titan Black (Kepler, sm\_35) under WSL2 / Ubuntu 24.04. Official PyPI wheels (1.12.1+cu113, +cu102) do NOT work anymore — Kepler kernels dropped from official builds (`CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device`). Only fix: compile from source. Working `.whl` produced and validated: `torch.cuda.is_available() == True`, matmul on GPU OK.

consulted.title: GPU Not Detected in PyTorch: Troubleshooting Guide GIGAGPU
consulted.content:
```
# Driver's maximum supported CUDA nvidia-smi | grep "CUDA Version" # PyTorch's compiled CUDA python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)"
```

The PyTorch CUDA version must not exceed the driver CUDA version. If it does, either upgrade your driver or install an older PyTorch build. See our tutorials for the compatibility matrix.

## Fix 3: Enable GPU Access in Docker [...] 1. CPU-only PyTorch installed. The default `pip install torch` may install the CPU build if no index URL is specified.
2. CUDA toolkit version mismatch. PyTorch was compiled against CUDA 12.1, but your driver only supports up to CUDA 11.8.
3. NVIDIA driver not loaded. The kernel module is missing or blacklisted.
4. Running inside a container without GPU passthrough. Docker needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. [...] If `nvidia-smi` itself fails, the issue is at the driver level — our guide on installing NVIDIA CUDA covers driver installation from scratch. If `nvidia-smi` works but `torch.version.cuda` prints `None`, you have a CPU-only PyTorch build.

## Fix 1: Replace CPU-Only PyTorch with GPU Build

This is the most common cause. Uninstall and reinstall with the correct CUDA index:

```
pip uninstall torch torchvision torchaudio -y pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url 
```
